title_cyr: Ајде слушај, слушај калеш бре Анѓо
title_latin: Ajde slušaj, slušaj kaleš bre Anǵo
background: A defiance song from Ottoman times, when Macedonia was under Turkish rule (roughly the late 1300s to 1912). A Turk courts Anǵa with promises: she will sit in a fine *čardak* (an enclosed upper balcony), count gold coins and string pearls for her neck. In the last verse she answers him: she won't be a Turkish wife, and she doesn't understand Turkish. Refusing marriage meant refusing conversion, so the song is remembered as a statement of faith and identity. *Kaleš* is a Turkish loanword, usually rendered "dark-eyed" or "black-haired". *Anama* means a Turkish lady or wife. Some versions add a verse where she says she would give her head before her faith.
background_source: Source of these notes: your 6-song songbook.

lines.cyr: Ајде слушај, слушај, калеш бре Анѓо,
lines.lat: Ajde slušaj, slušaj, kaleš bre Anǵo,

lines.en: The tambura is playing, black-haired Angja,
saying that you should be a wife of a Turk.

lines.cyr: Анама да бидиш, калеш бре Анѓо,
lines.lat: Anama da bidiš, kaleš bre Anǵo,
lines.en: You will be a wife of a Turk, black-haired Angja,
you will sit on the oriel.

lines.cyr: На чардак да седиш, калеш бре Анѓо,
lines.lat: Na čardak da sediš, kaleš bre Anǵo,
lines.en: You will sit on the oriel, black-haired Angja,

lines.cyr: Жолтици да броиш, калеш бре Анѓо,
lines.lat: Žoltici da broiš, kaleš bre Anǵo,
lines.en: You will count gold coins, black-haired Angja,

lines.cyr: Бисери да нижиш, калеш бре Анѓо,
lines.lat: Biseri da nižiš, kaleš bre Anǵo,
lines.en: You will weave pearls, black-haired Angja,
you will put them on your neck.

lines.cyr: Ајде, слушај, слушај клето бре Турче,
lines.lat: Ajde, slušaj, slušaj kleto bre Turče,
lines.en: Come on, listen, you damned Turk,
I will not be your wife.

lines.cyr: Анама не бивам, клето бре Турче,
lines.lat: Anama ne bivam, kleto bre Turče,
lines.en: I will not be your wife, you damned Turk,
